correctness.rationale: The quantified forcing condition yields component-constant successor rows and exactly \(2^{n\kappa(G)}\) modal relations. With equivalence accessibility it is equivalent to \(Q\subseteq M\), giving an exact weighted partition count. A spanning-forest rank inequality bounds all \(r\geq3\) terms at \(O(n^6 2^{-3n})\); partition cross-edge estimates bound all non-singleton first defects at \(O(n^2 2^{-3n/2})\). Therefore the two full asymptotic expansions and conditional rare-event descriptions follow. The standard-library checker independently tests all original relation equations for \(n\leq3\) and both exact enumeration sums for \(n\leq6\); finite tests do not replace the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The unrestricted count is exactly a known random-cluster partition-function specialization and is not treated alone as an original mathematical theorem. Existing phase-transition statements for fixed cluster weight and sparse edge activity cannot directly give the sharp cluster weight exponential in frame size, \(p=1/2\) first-defect coefficient; more importantly they do not include the distinct equivalence-accessibility weighting. Generic high-q expansions might subsume the unrestricted arm; the combined inversion and conditional first-defect comparison remain the assessed target.

value.rationale: For a natural finite quantum-modal frame class, enforcing equivalence accessibility reverses generic compatibility geometry under uniform pair sampling. The two sharp rates and first-defect shape theorems distinguish finite-model prevalence beyond existence, qualitative connectedness, or a routine single-number table. The result can serve as a quantitative baseline for studying richer modal restrictions; it does not purport to model a physically natural probability distribution.
